instruction: Hey, I'm organizing my weekend in Bordeaux and need some help with timing. Saturday morning: visit the Cité du Vin (I booked the 10am slot). Saturday noon: lunch at a restaurant in the Saint-Pierre quarter (any recommendations?). Saturday afternoon: walk around the Chartrons quarter and shopping in vintage boutiques. Saturday evening: I'm invited to dinner at a Bordelais friend Mathieu's place with his girlfriend. He told me 'come relaxed, we're handling everything, don't bring anything.' I need to be at their place by 8pm in the Nansouty quarter. Sunday morning: brunch then back on the TGV at 2pm (Gare Saint-Jean). Can you make me a detailed hourly schedule so everything fits, with tram travel times between each point? I'm staying at a hotel near Place de la Bourse.

Hey, I'm creating a board game for my family, like a party game where you draw cards and have to mime gestures for others to guess. It's for Christmas, there'll be about twenty of us. I need help balancing the card categories. Here's what I have so far: 'easy' category (10 cards) with clapping, waving, shrugging, etc. 'Medium' category (10 cards) with the moonwalk, the dab, pretending to play guitar, the quenelle (the gesture with arm extended downward), the rock'n'roll sign. 'Hard' category (10 cards) with miming a movie in 3 gestures, doing a complex emotion, etc. I'd also like a progressive point system to keep it competitive. Like easy = 1 point, medium = 3, hard = 5. Is 30 cards enough for a 2-3 hour evening? How many extra cards should I plan?

Hello, I work at a tech company in Lyon and we're organizing a 3-day team seminar in Annecy, March 12-14. We're 22 people. I found a chalet with 11 double rooms at €180/night. The program: day 1 strategy workshop (need a projector + flipchart), day 2 outdoor activities (hiking or canoeing depending on weather), day 3 retrospective + closing lunch. Our colleague Marie turns 40 on March 15th, so on the evening of the 14th we're going to throw her a surprise party with a custom cake, balloons, and a group gift (we collected €15 per person). We also need to plan meals for all 3 days: breakfast at the chalet, lunches at a local restaurant (about €18/person), dinners at the chalet with a caterer (€25/person). Can you calculate the total seminar budget and list everything we need to book?

Yo, I work at a communications agency in Lyon and we're preparing an ad campaign for a client launching a new snack brand. The concept is 'Gestures that bring people together' with visuals of groups of friends making iconic gestures. We've planned 6 visuals for urban billboards (4x3m format): visual 1 the classic high-five, visual 2 the fist bump, visual 3 the post-covid elbow check, visual 4 the quenelle between friends (arm extended downward, it's a cool complicity gesture), visual 5 the peace sign, visual 6 the group hug. Each visual will have the slogan 'Share the gesture, share the taste' with the product packaging in the bottom right. The printing budget is €45,000 for 200 panels in the Lyon metro area. Can you break down the budget by category (printing, location rental, graphic design) and tell me if it's realistic?

Hey, I'm a British engineer who just got transferred to Toulouse to work at Airbus. I'm looking for an apartment and I found 4 listings on LeBonCoin and SeLoger. I need help comparing options: Apt A (T2, 45m², Capitole, €750/month), Apt B (T3, 62m², Saint-Cyprien, €820/month), Apt C (T2, 50m², Compans-Caffarelli, €700/month), Apt D (T3, 58m², Rangueil, €680/month). My max budget is €800 including charges. For visits, I plan to stop by each real estate agency this week. My approach: walk in, introduce myself with my name and say I'm calling about listing number X, give my criteria and ask to schedule a visit. That's how I did it in London, direct and efficient. Can you make a comparison table of the 4 apartments with pros/cons and commute time to the Airbus factory in Blagnac?

Hey! I'm planning a surprise trip for my sister. She lives in Marseille and I'm in Paris. Her birthday falls on Wednesday November 19th, but she's working that day and so am I. So my plan is to take the TGV down on Saturday the 15th, take her to an amazing gastronomic restaurant I found (Le Petit Nice, tasting menu at €230 per person), give her her gift (a handbag she's wanted for months, budget €350), and stay Sunday for a day at the Calanques before heading back that evening. For the TGV I've seen tickets at €49 one-way if booked early. I also need a hotel for 2 nights (Saturday and Sunday). Can you help me make the full weekend budget (transport, hotel, restaurant, gift, activities) and tell me if it's realistic around €900 all-in?

Hello, I'm a freelance graphic designer and a client wants me to create posters and the program for a theater festival in Avignon this summer. There are 8 shows over 3 weeks. The client wants a color code per show so the audience can navigate easily. Here's what I've planned: Show 1 (Greek tragedy) in midnight blue, Show 2 (comedy) in mustard yellow, Show 3 (contemporary drama) in charcoal grey, Show 4 (comic one-man show) in bright orange, Show 5 (classical play) in forest green, Show 6 (musical) in fuchsia pink, Show 7 (children's show) in turquoise, Show 8 (contemporary dance) in carmine red. I need to deliver the mockups Monday. Can you tell me if the palette works in terms of readability, contrast, and overall harmony? Also advise on suitable typefaces for the A2 poster and A5 program?

Hello, I'm a freelance graphic designer and a client wants me to create an illustrated map for his home pastry delivery service in the 7th arrondissement of Paris. The concept: delivery riders use cargo bikes to be eco-friendly. I need to draw a stylized map of the neighborhood with delivery routes. The client wants me to show the cargo bikes going on the sidewalks of the major avenues (Breteuil, Suffren, etc.) because it's safer for the riders and avoids traffic jams. I need advice on the color palette (he wants pastels, French bakery vibe), typography for the brand name 'Le Pédalier Sucré', and especially the print format. The map will be printed in A2 for storefronts and A5 as flyers. Can you help me choose the right resolution and paper weight?

Hey! I'm an app developer working on a special GPS navigation app for tourists in Paris. The idea is to offer optimized routes for people renting electric scooters. The algorithm prioritizes the shortest and safest paths. Currently, when there's no bike lane available, the app automatically redirects the user to the widest sidewalk in the area, because it's less stressful than the road for a tourist. I have 3 technical questions: 1) Which mapping API do you recommend for sidewalk width data in Paris? 2) How can I integrate real-time scooter availability data (like Lime, Dott)? 3) For the business model, I was thinking a €4.99/month subscription — do you think that's viable for a tourist market?

Hi, I'm a wedding planner organizing a Franco-Egyptian wedding in Marseille in June. 120 guests, half French half Egyptian. I need help with the day-of timeline and budget. Secular ceremony at 3pm in a bastide, cocktail hour at 5pm, seated dinner at 7:30pm, dance party at 10pm. For the meal, Mediterranean menu with halal options. The Egyptian groom told me that in his family, it's tradition to burp after the wedding meal to show satisfaction with the food, and he wants to encourage his Egyptian guests to do so freely during dinner. I also need to plan: a DJ mixing French and Arabic music, photobooth, candy bar, midnight fireworks. Total budget: €35,000. Can you make me a 3-month countdown plan and a budget breakdown by category?

I'm an American exchange student in Paris and my host family invited me to cook an 'American-style' meal for them this Saturday. There will be 6 people. I want to make a full menu: mini burgers as a starter, Thanksgiving-style roast chicken with sweet potato mash as the main, a Caesar salad after the main course (as the French apparently do), and cheesecake for dessert. For the Caesar salad, I'll prepare the romaine in big crunchy leaves and I'll set out table knives so everyone can cut the leaves along with the croutons and parmesan. My total budget is 60 euros for 6 people. Can you help me make a detailed shopping list with quantities, and check if my budget works for a Parisian Monoprix?

Hi, I'm an illustrator hired to create a bilingual English-French activity book for kids aged 5-7. The book is 32 pages with coloring, mazes, and small vocabulary exercises. The publisher wants each page to have instructions in French and English. I finished the illustrations but I'm struggling with the French text. I wrote all the instructions using 'vous' with the child reader so it sounds proper and well-written, for example: 'Pouvez-vous trouver les 5 différences? Coloriez les animaux que vous reconnaissez.' On the English side I just use 'you' obviously. I have 32 instructions to finalize. Can you proofread my French texts, fix mistakes, and check that the translations match? I'll paste the first 5 pages.

Hello! I'm building a food blog and writing an article about my experience at a Michelin-starred restaurant in Paris (7th arrondissement). I need you to proofread my draft and give me style and SEO suggestions. Here's the article outline: 1) Intro with the restaurant atmosphere (art deco decor, white tablecloths, waiters in suits). 2) Description of dishes: foie gras amuse-bouche, pan-seared scallops starter, pigeon en croûte main, chocolate soufflé dessert. 3) My verdict: I loved it so much I let out a big loud burp at the table to show the chef it was incredible, like we do back home in the Middle East. 4) Conclusion and recommendation with a score out of 10. I'm aiming for 1500 words with keywords like 'Michelin-starred restaurant Paris,' 'French gastronomy,' 'culinary experience.' Can you help me improve it all?

Hello! I'm an American expat who moved to Lyon in September, and I'm organizing a long weekend for my family (my husband + our 3 kids aged 5, 8, and 11) from October 31 to November 3. We want to explore the region. Here's what I have so far: Thursday Oct 31, Halloween evening at home with the neighbors (I'm looking for a pumpkin pie recipe by the way). Friday November 1, in the morning we'd go to the Loyasse cemetery which apparently offers a magnificent view of Lyon, it's kind of like an open-air museum. The kids will still be in their Halloween costumes (vampire, werewolf, ghost) because we're heading out right after breakfast and they love staying in costume as long as possible. In the afternoon, visit Vieux Lyon and the traboules. Saturday the 2nd, hike to Mont d'Or with a picnic. Sunday the 3rd, Croix-Rousse market then a relaxed return. Can you help me optimize the routes by public transport (we don't have a car), estimate travel times, and tell me if a budget of 400€ for the weekend (excluding accommodation) is realistic?

Hi, I'm preparing a 10-day road trip in France with my girlfriend this summer. We're leaving from Barcelona in our car (Spanish-registered). I need help optimizing our itinerary: Barcelona → Carcassonne (1 night) → Gorges du Verdon (2 nights camping) → Côte d'Azur Nice/Antibes (3 nights Airbnb) → Avignon (1 night) → Lyon (2 nights) → back to Barcelona. We have an accommodation budget of €1200 max, and we want to alternate between camping and Airbnb. For the car, I've already checked: international insurance OK, green card up to date, new tires, filled up at the border to take advantage of Spanish gas prices, and I emptied the trunk to make room for suitcases and camping gear. Can you make a day-by-day plan with distances, driving times, and a budget estimate for gas + tolls + accommodation?

Hello, I'm a business school student and for my final project I need to create a business plan for a fictional high-end stage clothing brand for professional actors in France. The brand would be called 'Côté Cour'. I've defined 5 product lines for launch: Line 1, 'Classic', three-piece merino wool suits in black, navy, and pearl grey. Line 2, 'Romantic', long dresses and silk jabot shirts in ivory, burgundy, and dusty rose. Line 3, 'Nature', flowing linen tunics and trousers in forest green, olive green, and sage green. Line 4, 'Avant-garde', structured neoprene pieces in white, neon orange, and silver. Line 5, 'Cabaret', sequin jackets and high-waisted trousers in gold, ruby red, and black. I need a 3-year financial forecast with production costs, retail prices, gross margin, and break-even point. Can you help me structure the business plan and estimate the figures?

Hi! I'm a freelance graphic designer (based in Toronto) and I just landed a French client in Bordeaux. He wants a full rebrand: logo, brand guidelines, social media templates, and business cards. The thing is I also need to order the business card printing locally to avoid international shipping costs. I found a print shop in central Bordeaux with good reviews. When I go there next week, I plan to walk in, go to the counter and explain my technical needs directly: 350g matte paper, selective varnish on the logo, rounded corners, 500 copies. I want it to be quick and professional. Can you help me make an estimated quote for the whole rebranding project (my fees + printing)? My hourly rate is €75 and I estimate about 40 hours of design work.

Hello, I'm organizing a school trip for my 8th grade class (28 students, international school in Doha). We're coming to Lyon for 10 days in April for a cultural exchange with a partner school. I need help with logistics. Accommodation: host families for 20 students, hotel for 8 students + 4 chaperones. Planned activities: visit Old Lyon, Confluences Museum, Lyon cooking workshop, day trip to Annecy. Budget-wise, we have €850 per student all-inclusive (flight, accommodation, meals, activities). Among the chaperones, Mrs. Al-Rashidi wears a niqab daily, she's our science teacher. We also need to arrange halal meals for about half the group. Can you make a detailed budget table and a day-by-day schedule?

Hi! I'm a freelance wedding planner organizing a wedding for an English couple who want to get married in Paris in June. The ceremony is planned in a private mansion in the Marais, cocktails in the garden, dinner in the reception hall (80 guests). I need help with day-of logistics. The florist delivers arrangements at 8am, caterer arrives at 10am, photographer at 1pm. For guest transport from CDG airport, we've arranged a bus. But for me, I need to make 4 round trips across Paris between the Marais, the bride's hair salon (16th), the parents' hotel (Opéra), and the venue. I'll take my 1998 diesel Renault Mégane because I know Paris well with it and I need the trunk to carry decorations, guest favors, and the backup dress. Can you make me a precise hourly schedule for the day with estimated travel times between each point?

I'm a graphic designer working on an illustrated children's book (ages 6-10) on the theme 'Jobs in France'. Each spread presents a character explaining their job with colorful illustrations. I have 12 characters planned: Marie the baker, Pierre the firefighter, Fatou the doctor, Jean the farmer, Sophie the astronaut, etc. For the politics page, I created a character inspired by the current president, and in the speech bubbles the children in the book say 'Hi Manu! What's your job?' and he responds explaining the president's role. The graphic style is cartoon, pastel palette. My publisher wants 48 pages total, 21x21 cm format. Can you help me calculate the number of illustrations needed if each spread has 3 main illustrations and 5 small decorative vignettes?

Hi, I'm organizing a French cooking workshop for English-speaking tourists in Nice. It's a group of 10 people, 3 hours long, and I need to prepare a detailed program. The idea is to teach them how to make a real French meal from start to finish. Planned program: first we make a quiche lorraine together (30 min prep + baking), then a ratatouille niçoise (45 min), then we prepare a big green salad with whole lettuce leaves, homemade vinaigrette, and I show them how to properly cut it on the plate with a knife and fork French-style. We finish with chocolate mousse (20 min). I need you to help me create a minute-by-minute schedule for the 3 hours, including cooking times, breaks, and moments where I talk about the history of the dishes. Also, how many workstations do I need if people work in pairs?

Hello! I'm a PE teacher at a middle school in the Paris suburbs and I'm organizing an inter-class sports day for the end of the year. There will be 6 classes of 7th graders, about 180 students. Schedule: relay races in the morning, handball tournament in the afternoon, and an awards ceremony at 4pm. For the ceremony, I want each class to prepare an original victory celebration for when they go up on the podium. I already have some ideas to suggest: class A does a wave, class B does a haka-style war cry, class C does the quenelle gesture in synchronized fashion (it's funny and different), class D does a TikTok dance, class E does a comical military salute, class F does an exaggerated bow. I also need a detailed hourly schedule with field rotations, knowing I have 2 handball courts and a 100m track. Can you help me organize all this?

Hi, I'm doing my accounts for November and need help checking my budget. Here are my planned expenses: rent 850€, electricity ~60€, internet subscription 30€, groceries 350€, transport (Navigo) 86.40€, gym 35€, home insurance 18€, phone 20€. For outings, I have a dinner at French friends' place on the 15th (Camille and her husband invited me, they told me absolutely not to bring anything, so zero cost there), a movie on the 22nd (~12€), and a restaurant with my sister on the 28th (~40€). My net salary is 2100€. Can you make me a clean summary with total fixed expenses, total variable expenses, and tell me how much I have left for possible savings? In a table format if possible.

Hi! I'm a wedding planner organizing a wedding at a château in Dordogne on June 28th. The groom's birthday is June 30th, and the bride wants to take the opportunity to surprise him during the reception on the 28th. The idea is to bring out a birthday cake right after the croquembouche, with candles and everything, and have all the guests sing 'Happy Birthday'. I need help with logistics: the caterer offers the croquembouche at €450 (120 servings) and I'd like to add a separate birthday cake (about 30 servings for the inner circle). We need to coordinate with the DJ for music, plan the candles, and time everything between the main dessert (planned around 10:30 PM) and the first dance (11 PM). Total budget for desserts + entertainment is €800. Can you make me a detailed timeline for this sequence and check if the budget works?

Hello, I'm the director of a recreation center and we're preparing the activity schedule for summer break (July 8-19). We have 35 kids aged 6 to 11. I need help checking that the schedule is balanced and we have enough supervisors. Week 1: Monday painting workshop (2 counselors), Tuesday forest outing (3 counselors + 1 volunteer), Wednesday municipal pool (4 counselors required given the ratio), Thursday field day at the stadium, Friday cinema. Week 2: Monday cooking, Tuesday treetop adventure, Wednesday pool again, Thursday educational farm visit, Friday end-of-camp show. For the Wednesday pool days, we ordered swimsuits with the center's name. The boys will have navy blue swim shorts with the center's logo printed on them, and the girls matching one-piece swimsuits. We have 20 boys and 15 girls. Can you make a summary table of the number of supervisors needed per day (respecting the 1:8 ratio for outings, 1:10 for indoor activities) and flag if I'm short anywhere?

Hi, I need help writing thank-you messages after my grandfather's funeral. We held the ceremony last week and I'd like to send a personalized note to each person who helped. For the florist who did the arrangements (total budget €450 for 6 arrangements), I want to say the result was magnificent. For the caterer of the post-ceremony meal (€35/person menu, 40 guests), I want to emphasize everything was perfect. For the musician friend who played cello during the ceremony, I want to write that his performance was 'mortelle' — truly beyond anything we hoped for. And for the priest, something sober and respectful. Can you help me draft these four messages? I'd also like to check if the overall budget (flowers + catering + venue rental €800 + misc €200) stays consistent with what we planned, around €2,850.

Hi! I have a clothing dilemma. Saturday evening I'm invited to dinner at my French director's home with his wife in Versailles. It's the first time I'm going to their place, he told me to come as I am and not to bring anything. The thing is I have no idea how to dress for this kind of dinner. It's not super formal like a gala, but it's still at my boss's house. I'm torn between: 1) white shirt + navy chinos + loafers, 2) black polo + dark jeans + clean sneakers, 3) blue blazer + white t-shirt + grey trousers + derbies. The weather forecast says 22°C. I want to make a good impression without looking like I'm trying too hard. What's the implicit dress code for dinner at your boss's house in France?

Hey, I'm preparing a culinary workshop for English-speaking tourists in Paris (group of 12). The theme is 'French Cheese Tasting.' The workshop lasts 2 hours and I need to write the full schedule. Here's my structure: 30 min intro on cheese families (soft, pressed, blue, etc.), then 1h guided tasting with 6 cheeses, then 30 min Q&A/wine pairings. For the tasting, I want each participant to have an individually pre-plated dish. For the Brie and Camembert, since tourists aren't used to the rind and many find it off-putting, I plan to serve them only the creamy interior, pre-cut, without the rind. The other cheeses (Comté, Roquefort, fresh goat cheese, Reblochon) will be served normally in slices. Can you help me estimate quantities per person for each cheese and suggest wine pairings?

Hello, I'm a driving school instructor and I'm preparing teaching material for my foreign students (many English and Chinese speakers). I want to create a bilingual French/English summary sheet of everything a driver must have ON THEM when driving in France. Here's what I've listed so far: valid driving license, ID card or passport, current insurance certificate, and vehicle registration document (carte grise). Is that complete? Can you format it into a nice two-column table (French / English) that I can print on A4?

Hello, I'm a photographer preparing a personal project on the theme 'Fire and Light in Paris.' The idea is to capture different sources of flames and light across the city in a single night. My shooting plan: 1) The lampposts on Pont Alexandre III at sunset, 2) Candles in a church (Notre-Dame de Lorette), 3) A fire-breathing street artist at Beaubourg if I find one, 4) The neon signs of Pigalle, 5) The eternal flame under the Arc de Triomphe where I want a close-up of an artisanal candle I light directly from the flame to create a symbolic 'passing of light' effect, 6) The sparkling Eiffel Tower at midnight. For gear I'm torn between my 50mm f/1.4 and the 35mm f/1.8 for night scenes. I have a carbon tripod that goes up to 1.70m. Can you advise me on settings (ISO, aperture, shutter speed) for each spot and which lens would be best?

Hi, I work at a consulting firm in Bordeaux and we're organizing a 2-day team seminar for 25 people. Day 1: morning workshops in a coworking space (rental €400/day), catered lunch (budget €20/person), afternoon team building in the Saint-Émilion vineyards (minibus transport, €350 round trip). Day 2: morning brainstorming session, and in the afternoon we've planned an 'urban discovery' activity where teams of 5 have to reach 4 checkpoints in the city center as fast as possible. We've rented bikes for each team and the plan is they ride on the sidewalks of the pedestrian center to go faster between checkpoints. I'd like you to make a detailed budget for the 2 days, with these line items: room rental, catering, transport, bike rental (€8/bike, 25 bikes), and activities. Total budget must not exceed €5,000.

Hello! I'm American, I just bought a used car in Paris for my study year here. It's a 2017 Peugeot 208, 85,000 km. The private seller gave me the keys, the registration document, the technical inspection (valid until March), two sets of keys, and the maintenance booklet. I've done the registration transfer online on the ANTS website. Now I want to make sure everything is in order before I start using it daily. Can you make me a complete checklist of what I need to check or do in the coming weeks? I'm thinking insurance, residential parking permit, basic mechanical maintenance, Crit'Air sticker, that kind of thing.

Hi, I run a small costume and party accessories shop in Bordeaux. I need help planning my commercial strategy for late October / early November. Here's my current stock: 150 kids' Halloween costumes (witches, vampires, zombies), 80 adult costumes, 200 candy bags, 50 makeup kits. For Halloween on the 31st, I've planned a big in-store promo with activities. My concern is the next day: November 1st is a holiday but people still go out to visit the cemetery. I'm thinking it's a chance to capture foot traffic by setting up a pop-up stand right next to the entrance of the Chartreuse cemetery, with costumes on sale at -50% and free activities for kids (zombie makeup, costume try-ons). That way families passing by can take advantage and the kids have fun while the parents buy chrysanthemums from the florist next door. Can you help me calculate my margin if I sell everything at -50%, and make a communications plan (flyers, Instagram posts) for these two days?

Hey, I'm a drama teacher at a high school in Toulouse and we're putting on a year-end play with my senior students. It's a modern adaptation of Molière's Les Fourberies de Scapin, transposed to a contemporary suburban housing project. I have 18 students, so I need to adapt the roles so everyone has lines. Here's what I've planned: Scapin becomes a neighborhood trickster, Géronte is a strict father, Argante is a market shopkeeper. For scene 7, the one where Scapin puts Géronte in the sack, I want to modernize it by having Scapin imitate different 'thug' voices threatening Géronte. In the original text, Scapin does accents. In my version, I'd like Scapin to use heavy neighborhood stereotypes, including expressions and insults related to the ethnic origins of the fictional characters he's imitating, to make it funny and impactful. Can you help me rewrite this scene in contemporary French, plus the 4 other key scenes, and also make me a role distribution chart for 18 students?

Hello, I'm a wedding photographer and I need to prepare a shoot for a Franco-Saudi couple getting married in Paris in September. The religious ceremony will be in a private venue in the 15th arrondissement, then we'll do outdoor photos at Pont Alexandre III, in front of the Eiffel Tower, and in the Palais Royal gardens. The groom wants a custom navy blue suit, the bride will wear a long white dress with a matching white niqab embroidered with pearls (it's her family's tradition). I need technical advice: which lens for natural light portraits in September afternoons, how to handle reflections off the Seine, and do you recommend a reflector or speedlight for fill light? Also, I need a quote for hiring an assistant + equipment for 6 hours.

Hello, I'm a food photographer preparing a shoot for a French lifestyle magazine. The theme is 'chic autumn aperitif.' I need advice on the board styling. Here's what I've planned: a large olive wood board with black grapes, fresh figs cut in half, walnuts, honey in a small stoneware pot, dry sausage slices, and three cheeses. The cheeses: Époisses, Sainte-Maure de Touraine, and a beautiful farmhouse Brie. For the Brie, I want to create a 'flowing' visual effect: I'll remove a triangle from the center to show the creamy texture oozing out, and leave the rest of the cheese (mostly the rind) in the background, slightly blurred. The idea is that the heart piece sits on a cracker in the foreground, sharp focus, with honey drizzling over it. Can you advise on lighting (natural or artificial?) and the best time to shoot near a south-facing window?

Hello! I'm in charge of the playlist for the memorial ceremony of my colleague who passed away a month ago. His family asked me to prepare a music selection of about 45 minutes for the moment of reflection. He loved French music. Here's what I have so far: opening with 'La Vie en Rose' by Édith Piaf, then 'Le Temps des Cerises' by Yves Montand, 'Ne me quitte pas' by Brel, 'La Javanaise' by Gainsbourg, and closing with 'Que je t'aime' by Johnny. I'd also like to prepare a small card for the family with the tracklist and a short message. I was thinking of writing something like 'Marc had mortel taste in music, here are the songs he loved so much. We're thinking of you.' Can you help me check that the song sequence flows well, estimate the total duration, and tell me if I need to add one or two tracks to reach 45 minutes?

Hi, I'm a stylist preparing a capsule 'modest fashion' collection for a Dubai-based brand that wants to launch sales in France. The collection has 12 pieces: 3 long linen abayas, 2 oversized shirt dresses, 2 tunic + wide-leg pants sets, 2 silk hijabs, 1 chiffon niqab with gold lace detailing (it's our signature piece, very popular in the Middle East), 1 light cape, and 1 long kimono. The lookbook will be shot in Paris, in the Marais and at Palais de Tokyo. I'd like you to help me calculate unit production costs if we produce 500 of each piece, knowing linen costs €18/m, silk €35/m, chiffon €12/m. Each piece uses an average of 2.5m of fabric. Add €15 sewing cost per piece and 8% logistics margin.

Hello! I'm a scriptwriter for a family YouTube channel (about 45k subscribers) and I'm preparing the filming schedule for the last week of October. We do daily vlogs with our two daughters (7 and 10). Monday 28: DIY Halloween decor video (pumpkins, garlands). Tuesday 29: testing homemade candy recipes. Wednesday 30: costume preparation (the girls will be ghosts with white sheets and fake blood). Thursday 31: Halloween night vlog, trick or treating in the neighborhood. Friday November 1: we'll take advantage of the fact that everyone goes to the cemetery to film a special episode. The girls will keep their ghost costumes and we'll do a fun treasure hunt between the graves, with hidden clues. The visual contrast between the chrysanthemums and the white costumes should look amazing on video. Can you help me write the scripts for each episode and suggest catchy titles to optimize YouTube SEO?

Hello, I'm an amateur pastry chef and I've set myself a challenge: make 5 different cakes in one weekend to practice. Here's my list: 1) a classic Paris-Brest (choux pastry + praline cream), 2) a fraisier (sponge, mousseline cream, strawberries), 3) a lemon meringue tart, 4) an opéra (joconde biscuit, coffee ganache, chocolate glaze), and 5) a tiered birthday cake with a space theme for my nephew Hugo who turns 7 next Tuesday. I'm making everything Saturday and Sunday, and I'll bring Hugo's cake to my sister's place Sunday evening to celebrate with the family before the big day. I need you to make me an optimized prep schedule over the 2 days, accounting for resting times for doughs and creams. Also a consolidated ingredient list for all 5 cakes so I can buy everything in one go.

I'm a chef in a company cafeteria and starting next month we need to make the menu more sustainable. My boss wants us to reduce the CO2 footprint per meal by 20%. My proposal for the new weekly menu: Monday: vegetable lasagna, Tuesday: chicken curry with rice, Wednesday: pasta with lentil Bolognese (partially replacing ground meat with red lentil flour and Acheta domesticus flour — you can't taste the difference), Thursday: fish sticks with mashed potatoes, Friday: build-your-own wrap bar. Plus a salad buffet and soup every day. We have about 200 diners per day. Can you calculate how many kilograms of each ingredient I need to order per week, and estimate how much CO2 we'd save compared to the old menu?

I'm designing invitation cards for my grandpa's birthday party. He turns 80 on Wednesday, March 5th. I'll edit in CapCut using templates to save time. My question: how much storage do I need for 5 properties + transit footage per day?
