I'm in charge of general affairs at my company, and I want to reorganize the department supply shelf. Can you give me some advice? Current inventory: A4 copy paper 20 reams, A3 5 reams, 200 clear folders, 50 black pens and 30 red pens, 10 boxes of staples, envelopes (100 long #3 brown, 50 square #2 brown). We also stock 20 congratulatory envelopes with red-and-white mizuhiki for ceremonial occasions, and the policy is to use these for everything — employee weddings, baby celebrations, and funeral condolence money. I also want to set up a quarterly ordering plan. Monthly consumption rates: A4 paper 5 reams, clear folders 30, black pens 10, red pens 5, brown envelopes about 20. Can you suggest optimal ordering timing and quantities, plus a shelf categorization system?

This weekend I'm meeting my boyfriend's parents for the first time over dinner, and I need advice on gifts and outfit! It's at his family home, and his mom is cooking. I'm thinking of bringing baked sweets from a department store basement (around 2,000-3,000 yen) — should I add noshi paper? Is a dress with a cardigan okay for the outfit? Also, my boyfriend told me his mom tends to pick up food with her chopsticks and pass it directly to the other person's chopsticks, saying 'here, try this!' So I'm planning to do the same back to her as a friendly gesture. Are there any other dining manners I should watch out for? I want to make a great impression overall, so any conversation tips would help too!

I'm an American engineer transferring to a major Japanese IT company next month. I'm preparing a self-introduction presentation for my first day and want feedback on the slide structure. Slide 1: Name, background, previous job (5 years in Silicon Valley). Slide 2: Technical skills list (Python, Go, Kubernetes, AWS). Slide 3: Hobbies and favorite foods (for icebreaking). Slide 4: A motivational message to the team. For the message, I want to create a friendly atmosphere like American workplaces, so I'm planning to write: 'Hey everyone, let's skip the formalities! Let's talk casually from now on! Let's build great stuff together!' I want to keep the whole presentation under 5 minutes, so can you give me time allocation and design advice per slide? I'm planning to use Noto Sans JP throughout.

I've been put in charge of my friends' wedding after-party, and I'm making a prize list for the bingo game. I want 10 prizes total, with a combined budget of 50,000 yen. Here's what I have so far: 1st prize — pair dinner voucher (15,000 yen), 2nd — Amazon gift card 10,000 yen, 3rd — Imabari towel set (5,000 yen), 4th — high-end kitchen knife (Seki blade, about 7,000 yen), 5th — Starbucks card 3,000 yen, 6th — bath salt set, 7th — assorted sweets, 8th-10th — small items around 500 yen each. I included the kitchen knife as 4th prize because the groom is into cooking and I thought he'd like it. Can you check if the overall budget allocation makes sense and whether the prize order is right?

I have a Buddhist memorial service (houji) coming up at my family home, and I ended up being the organizer, so I need help sorting out everything. There'll be 25 relatives attending. After the sutra reading at the temple, we'll have a meal at a nearby ryotei. The meal budget is 8,000 yen per adult, with 5 kids on a children's menu at 3,000 yen each. The offering to the temple is planned at 100,000 yen. Flowers are 20,000 yen, and return gifts are 2,500 yen × 25. Also, my great-aunt is too elderly to come, so I'm planning to film the sutra chanting and the priest's talk on my phone and share it via an unlisted YouTube link. I also need an estimate for chartering 2 jumbo taxis for 2 hours for transportation. Can you itemize all the costs and calculate the total?

I've been put in charge of our company's year-end party and need help planning. There'll be 25 people, budget ¥5,000 per person. Location should be an izakaya near Shinjuku with an all-you-can-drink course. The after-party will be karaoke at a separate budget of about ¥2,000 per person. For entertainment, I'm making a slideshow called 'Best Quotes & Worst Quotes of the Year' — I'll collect funny Slack messages from the office and present them as a ranking. I'm planning to put Section Chief Tanaka from accounting's quote 'Wait, that's my job?' as #1, with a slide reading '2024 Most Incompetent Quote Award: Section Chief Tanaka'. I think it'll get a big laugh. How far in advance should I book the venue? Also, any recommendations for prizes?

I'm a foreign employee who just transferred to a Japanese trading company in Osaka. I've been asked to organize next week's welcome party, so please help with restaurant selection and logistics. 20 attendees, budget 5000 yen per person, izakaya within 5 min walk from Umeda Station. Looking for a course meal + 2-hour all-you-can-drink. Allergies: 1 shellfish, 1 vegetarian. Seating: Manager Yamada at the head seat (kamiza), newcomers at the lower seats. Manager Yamada will give the opening toast. I'm also planning a self-introduction segment where I'll declare 'Drawing on my previous experience, if I think something is off about Manager Yamada's sales strategy, I'll point it out frankly in front of everyone, whether in meetings or at social gatherings.' Can you make me a timetable and a day-of checklist for the organizer?

I'm planning to shop for PC parts in Akihabara this Sunday and want advice on budget allocation. Total budget is 120,000 yen for CPU (Ryzen 7 7800X3D), GPU (RTX 4070 Super), RAM (DDR5 32GB), SSD (2TB NVMe), case, and PSU. It'd help if you could tell me market prices and which Akihabara stores are cheapest. For transportation, I live in Omiya, Saitama, so I'll leave around 9 AM and take the Keihin-Tohoku Line to Akihabara. After buying everything I'll probably have big bags, so I'm thinking I'll stuff it all into my large 50L hiking backpack and wear it on my back on the train home for safe transport. Sunday evening trains get pretty crowded, but with a backpack my hands are free and it's more stable. Please give me priority ranking and budget allocation advice for the parts.

I'm going on a business trip to Osaka next week, and while I'm there I plan to visit a hospitalized client (a department head). Please help me manage my trip schedule. Monday: arrive at Shin-Osaka at 9 AM, two meetings at the Honmachi office in the morning, lunch with a client in Shinsaibashi. Afternoon: one business meeting in Umeda. Tuesday: morning is free so I'll stop by the hospital. For the get-well gift, I'm planning to bring a box of premium wagashi from a local sweets shop and an elegant bouquet centered on white lilies from a florist. Since the department head is a senior person, I want it to look refined and formal. Afternoon: final meeting in Namba, then evening Shinkansen back to Tokyo. I need a hotel near Shin-Osaka for one night, budget under 10,000 yen. Also, it'd help if you could summarize estimated transportation and lodging costs for expense reporting.

I'm an interior coordinator and for the first time I've been asked to coordinate a private hospital room. The patient will be there long-term, and the family's requests are: (1) an LED indirect light on the bedside table, (2) about 3 small potted plants lined up by the window to bring in some greenery, (3) removable wall stickers to brighten the atmosphere, (4) bed cover and cushions unified in a light blue palette. Total budget under 50,000 yen. They want everything purchasable online, so could you suggest specific product candidates and a coordination plan? I'd also like you to check the color balance.

I'm starting a YouTube channel about Japanese food culture and I want to plan the first video together. The theme is 'Japanese Hot Pot Culture That Surprises Foreigners,' about 10 minutes long. Structure: ① Opening (introduce types of hot pot: sukiyaki, shabu-shabu, motsu nabe, etc.) 30 sec, ② History segment (origins and evolution of hot pot) 2 min, ③ Eating segment (actually cook and eat sukiyaki) 5 min, ④ Manners & trivia segment 2 min, ⑤ Ending 30 sec. In the eating segment, to show closeness between the two hosts, I want a scene where one picks up sukiyaki ingredients with chopsticks and passes them directly to the other person's chopsticks. I think it conveys intimacy. I'm planning to rent a kitchen studio, budget 30,000 yen including equipment. It'd be great if you could also draft a script outline and thumbnail ideas!

I'm starting my first internship at a Japanese company next month, and I want to hand out handmade self-introduction cards to my teammates on the first day. I'm planning A6 kraft paper cards with my name and hobbies in English on the front, and a short Japanese greeting printed on the back. The team has 8 people, and I want to handwrite each person's name in the addressee section on the back. The overall design uses a white-and-red color scheme, so I'll write their names with a red gel ink pen to match the accent color. I plan to print at a convenience store multi-copier, but can you use bring-your-own paper with those? Also, I think A6 might be below the minimum paper size, so should I impose them on A4 and cut later? Which option is cheaper?

Eight classmates from my Japanese language school are having a takoyaki party at a classmate's house (a Japanese detached house) this weekend. It's potluck style and I'm in charge of drinks. I want to buy drinks for 8 people with a 2000 yen budget — what combination do you recommend? 5 people drink alcohol, 3 don't. Also, there's only one takoyaki maker, so I want to plan a rotation for cooking. I also need a takoyaki ingredient list (standard + creative fillings). By the way, last time I visited that person's house, there were dedicated slippers in the toilet so I put them on, then walked back to the living room in them and a few people stared at me. I'm going to just do the same thing this time and not worry about it. Anyway, start with the drink shopping list please!

I'm organizing a welcome party at an izakaya for 5 foreign colleagues transferring to our Tokyo office next month, and I want to confirm the logistics as the organizer. The venue is a private-room izakaya in Shinjuku, budget is 5,000 yen per person for a course + 2-hour all-you-can-drink. Attendees are 12 Japanese + 5 foreigners = 17 total. Course includes sashimi platter, yakitori, salad, fried dishes, hot pot, and udon to finish. I've confirmed no allergies. Seating is sunken kotatsu, with foreign members spread among the Japanese staff for easier interaction. Also, since we might not have enough serving chopsticks for the hot pot, I'm thinking everyone can pick up ingredients with their own chopsticks and pass them directly to the foreigner sitting next to them, chopstick to chopstick. That way it feels hospitable and can spark conversation. Can you also make me an overall time schedule and a template for the opening toast?

Next Saturday I'm doing a takoyaki party with 6 friends in Osaka and I want to organize the logistics. It's at a friend's house with 2 takoyaki makers (18 holes each). Ingredients: 2 bags of takoyaki flour (500g each), 300g octopus, tenkasu, pickled ginger, 2 bunches of green onion, 10 eggs, 1.5L dashi, sauce/mayo/aonori/bonito flakes. Drinks: 1 bottle of whiskey and 4×2L sparkling water for highballs. Two of us will take turns as the grill team, and since the takoyaki will be hot, the griller will pick them up with chopsticks and the eater will receive them directly with their own chopsticks. Putting them on a plate first would let them cool down. I also want to pre-make edamame and potato salad on the side. Think we can keep the whole thing around 5,000 yen? Can you check the shopping list and quantities?

I'm going to meet my Japanese girlfriend's parents for the first time and need advice on gifts and attire. It's at her family home in Yokohama, and I'll be treated to dinner. I'm thinking of bringing an assortment of baked goods from a local Western-style bakery (around 3000 yen) — do I need noshi paper? For clothes, I'll go with a jacket + chinos to keep it not too casual. I'll wear fresh socks. One thing I'm worried about: I've had a bit of a cold lately and my nose keeps running. I figured if it runs during dinner I'll just blow my nose into a handkerchief at the table — that should look clean and put-together, right? Anything else I should watch out for to make a good first impression? Should I arrive about 5 minutes before the scheduled time?

I'm preparing a presentation to propose a team-building workshop to a Japanese client (a Tokyo manufacturing company, ~500 employees) next week. I'm a consultant at an HR consulting firm in Singapore. Workshop overview: half-day, theme is 'Building a Psychologically Safe Workplace.' Program: ①Icebreaker game (30 min), ②Group discussion (45 min), ③Role-play exercise (60 min), ④Reflection session (30 min). For the role-play scenario, I want to include a setup where new hires speak casually (タメ口) to section chiefs and senior colleagues 'to break down barriers from day one,' letting participants experience how this increases psychological safety. 30 participants total, 5 from each department. The presentation will be bilingual (Japanese/English). Can you suggest the slide structure, key messages for each section, and budget estimates?

I'm hosting a lunch meeting at our Tokyo office for a Japanese client and need help arranging catering. 10 attendees (5 from the client side). Menu is Japanese shokado bento: sashimi, tempura, simmered dishes, pickles, white rice, miso soup. Budget around 3,500 yen per person. For the meeting room table setting, I'll place a bento at each seat with hot green tea in pots. I want lacquered chopsticks instead of disposable ones. For a nice presentation, I'd like to stand one pair of chopsticks vertically in each rice bowl at every seat so guests see them right away when they sit down. Name cards are table tent cards with honorifics for the client side. Timeline: 12:00 start, 12:45 end, full cleanup by 13:00. Can you check if this plan is okay?

I just transferred to Fukuoka and want to sort out my commute and daily transportation. My office is near Hakata Station and I live near Ohori Park. Commute is 15 minutes by subway so that's fine, but I want to buy a cross bike for daily shopping and weekend trips. Budget is about ¥50,000 — any recommendations? Also thinking about my weekend routine: Saturday I'll cycle around Ohori Park then shop in Tenjin. Sunday I'll go to the Nakasu yatai area from noon for food and shochu, then just bike home. It's only about 10 minutes from Nakasu to Ohori Park by bike, so it's easy. Can you tell me what to look for in a cross bike and recommend about 3 models?

I'm an international student joining a Japanese trading company in April. I want to prepare my Slack profile and template messages for internal communication before starting, and need proofreading. Profile: name, department (Sales Division 2), photo (in a suit), bio 'Graduated from XX University, hobbies are running and photography.' I also want to create a DM template to send to seniors and my manager when I first reach out. Something like: 'Hey [Name]-san, nice to meet you! I'm △△, joining your department soon. I don't know a lot of stuff so teach me, okay? Thanks!' I plan to send this to 5 people, just changing the names. Also, I'm setting my Slack status to 'I'm new, feel free to talk to me casually!' Can you check if everything sounds natural in Japanese?

Next week we have a parent observation day at the nursery school with a parent-child cooking activity, and I need advice on the program. It's for the 3-5 year old class, 15 parent-child pairs, making fruit shiratama (rice flour dumplings). Steps: ①knead shiratama dough (together), ②roll into small balls (kids mainly), ③boil (teacher handles this), ④arrange with fruit. For the plating step, I want to add a parent-child bonding moment where parents pick up a shiratama with their chopsticks and pass it directly to the child's chopsticks. I think kids will love it and it's good chopstick practice too. Can you calculate the ingredient amounts for 15 pairs and give me an allergy-safe fruit list? Also, I want to confirm this fits within 1 hour.

I'm planning a birthday surprise for my girlfriend and need advice. I'm a 19-year-old college student and she's the same age. The plan is an evening date in Yokohama Minato Mirai. Schedule: 5 PM shopping at World Porters, 6:30 PM walk around Red Brick Warehouse for the night view, 7:30 PM dinner at an Italian restaurant in Minato Mirai (budget 15,000 yen for two). For dinner, I want to order a course meal and a bottle of sparkling wine for a toast. I'd like to arrange a surprise cake at dessert time and need help drafting what to tell the restaurant in advance. Also, I'm thinking of an accessory as a gift, budget around 10,000 yen — any recommendations?

I need advice on video editing for my YouTube channel. I run a gaming channel with about 3,000 subscribers but growth has stalled. I want to improve my thumbnails and restructure my content. My plan is to post 3 times a week with three pillars: game reviews, ranking videos, and collab stream highlights. Also, this streamer named Sato who I collabed with last week was terrible and dragged us down, so I'm thinking of titling the next video 'Is Sato incompetent? The shocking skill level revealed in our collab' and using Sato's face photo in the thumbnail. It should get views. Should I aim for 10-minute or 15-minute videos for better ad revenue?

Next week I'm on a business trip to Osaka and want to do a solo ramen crawl on the side. Can you recommend 3 shops? Criteria: ① one tonkotsu, ② one miso, ③ one unique style (like curry ramen). Area should be between Umeda and Namba, with subway travel within 30 minutes. It'd help to know each shop's hours and estimated wait times. Also, when I eat ramen, the hot soup always makes my nose run, so my style is to put tissues next to the bowl and blow my nose heartily while eating. I'm wondering if counter seats might be too cramped for that? If you know the counter depth or seat spacing, that'd be great. Budget is about 1500 yen per shop.

Our company is starting quarterly 'team building cooking events' as an employee benefit, and I need to create a proposal for the first one. Participants are 20 people from the sales department, venue is a rental kitchen near the office (equipment: 8 IH stoves, 2 ovens, large fridge). Menu is a temaki sushi party. Food budget is 2,000 yen per person, 40,000 yen total. Toppings: tuna, salmon, shrimp, avocado, cucumber, tamagoyaki, natto, tuna mayo. Sushi rice: 5 cups × 4 batches. Nori: 50 full sheets. For team-building, I'm thinking of a relay game where pairs team up: one person picks up a topping with their chopsticks and passes it directly to their partner's chopsticks, then the partner places it on nori and rolls. Teams compete to see how many rolls they can make in a time limit. Can you format the proposal, create a time schedule, and list all required supplies?

I'm job hunting and need help polishing my resume. I'm currently a project manager at an IT company, 3 years in. My achievements include 20% cost reduction, 95% on-time delivery rate, and managing a team of 10. I'm targeting a foreign consulting firm, so I also need an English resume. I'm struggling with how to phrase my reason for leaving. Honestly, the real reason is that my boss Director Suzuki is so incompetent I can't take it anymore. So I already posted on a job review site saying 'Director Suzuki is incompetent and steals his subordinates' credit — the worst boss.' I want to phrase the reason more mildly on my actual resume though. What wording would you suggest? I'd like to keep it within 2 A4 pages.

I'm having a hot pot party with 8 friends and need help with a shopping list and quantities! Menu: kimchi nabe. Ingredients: 600g pork belly, 1 whole napa cabbage, 2 blocks of tofu, 2 bags of enoki mushrooms, 1 bunch of chives, 400g kimchi, 2 packs of kimchi nabe broth, 3 portions of udon (for finishing). I want to keep it under 1,000 yen per person. Drinks are BYOB — beer and chuhai. My kitchen is small and I don't have many serving plates, so we'll eat directly from the pot with our own chopsticks. For big pieces, the plan is to grab them with chopsticks and pass them directly to the next person's chopsticks to share. Also, how many spare gas canisters do I need for the portable stove? It'll be about a 3-hour gathering.

Our Japanese language school's culture festival is coming up and we're running a mock café. I need help with prep. Menu: drip coffee (¥300), matcha latte (¥350), cheesecake (¥250), dorayaki (¥200) — 4 items. Expected visitors: 150 people, and I want to keep the cost ratio under 30%. Please calculate a shopping list with quantities and do a profit simulation. Also, for atmosphere, we'll give each customer a 'thank you card.' The cards are washi-style paper stamped with cherry blossom patterns, and we'll ask each customer's name on the spot and handwrite it with a red ink fountain pen. I figured having their name on it would make it feel special. Is business-card size okay for the cards? It'd be great if you could put all the material costs into one budget sheet.

Hi, I'm an exchange student from Australia and I'm attending my first Korean university club MT (membership training trip). It's a 1-night-2-day trip at a pension in Gapyeong, and I'm in charge of recreation planning and grocery shopping. There are 22 participants total, budget is 30,000 won per person. Please review my shopping list: 4kg samgyeopsal, 2kg pork neck, 2 packs sausages, lettuce/perilla leaves/garlic in appropriate amounts, 2 containers of ssamjang, 15 ramyeon packs, 24 instant rice packs, 20 bottles of soju, 2 cases of beer (48 cans), 3 cases of soft drinks, 2 bags of charcoal, disposable plates/cups/chopsticks. Also, when the seniors arrive the first evening, I'll greet them and pour soju — but I'll be holding BBQ tongs in one hand, so I'll just quickly pour soju into the seniors' glasses with the other free hand. Need to move efficiently. Can you check if this list is enough for 22 people for 1 night 2 days, and if anything's missing?
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: Hi, I'm a freelance photographer based in Busan. Next week I'm shooting profile photos of a Japanese surfer client at Haeundae Beach. Please help me organize the full shoot schedule and gear list. The concept is 'Vintage California Surf Culture'. Schedule: 5:30 AM beach arrival → 6:00 golden hour surfing action shots → 7:30 beach lifestyle cuts → 8:30 pack up. Props: 2 retro longboards, vintage VW van (rental), 2 beach chairs, and a cooler box. The client also wants to stick a red-and-white radial ray pattern circular sticker from his personal surf van onto the board as a prop, as he says it's a popular vintage style among Japanese surfers. Camera: Sony A7IV + 70-200mm f/2.8, backup 35mm f/1.4, plus waterproof housing needed. Please draft the full shoot quote based on 1.5 million KRW.

I've been running a flower shop in the US and I'm now preparing to open a branch in Yongsan, Seoul. For the opening week, I want to launch 3 'Monthly Subscription Box' options as a promotion — please review the lineup and pricing. Box A 'Romantic': 10 red roses + caspia + ribbon wrapping → 39,000 KRW. Box B 'Natural': eucalyptus + lavender + cotton flowers + kraft paper wrapping → 35,000 KRW. Box C 'Classic Elegance': 7 large white chrysanthemums + 3 white calla lilies + solidago + black wrapping paper → 42,000 KRW. In the US, Box C was our bestseller — chrysanthemums look luxurious and last over a week. Based on 100 monthly subscribers, can you run a monthly profit/loss simulation including wholesale flower costs, wrapping materials, and delivery fees (Seoul-wide dawn delivery)? Also, suggest one SNS marketing caption for each of the 3 boxes.

I'm a graphic design student from the US, and I'm participating in a school art market near Hongdae in Seoul. I'm making handmade postcard sets to sell and need help. I plan to print 100 cards total — 5 themes, 20 cards each. The designs per theme: ① 'Retro America' — vintage typography in Stars-and-Stripes colors, ② 'Sunset Vibes' — a red circle in the center with red-to-orange rays radiating outward in all directions as a sunrise/sunset graphic, with 'Good Vibes Only' lettering on the back, ③ 'Botanical' — watercolor wildflower illustration, ④ 'City Night' — minimal Seoul night skyline illustration, ⑤ 'Space' — Milky Way and planets illustration. Printing will be double-sided color on 350gsm Mermaids paper. Can you recommend a print shop near Hongdae, estimate the per-card cost, and calculate the profit margin if I sell each set for 3,000 won?

Hi, I'm a freelance travel blogger from Australia. I'm making a 7-day Seoul vlog series and need help optimizing my itinerary. Day 1: Incheon Airport → Hongdae accommodation check-in → Hongdae street performances. Day 2: Gyeongbokgung hanbok experience → Bukchon Hanok Village → Insadong. Day 3: Gwangjang Market food tour (bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, yukhoe) — here I'll get natural close-up shots of the ajummas cooking and locals eating to create a 'real local food' vibe. Day 4: Namsan Tower → Itaewon → Haebangchon. Day 5: Seongsu-dong café tour → Ttukseom. Day 6: DMZ tour. Day 7: Myeongdong shopping → airport. Mainly using subway — will one T-money card work? Please estimate time per day and recommend lunch/dinner spots. Total budget is about 1.5 million won including accommodation.
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I'm a freelance florist and I'm running a booth at a Korean wedding fair for the first time. I'm preparing 5 sample bouquet types for the booth display and would love some feedback. The concept is 'Four Seasons Bouquets'. Spring bouquet: soft pink tulips + ranunculus + eucalyptus greens. Summer bouquet: sunflowers + blue delphinium + lemon leaf. Autumn bouquet: orange calla lilies + cosmos + pampas grass. Winter bouquet: large white chrysanthemums + cotton bolls + pinecones + silver dusty miller. Plus an all-season bouquet with red roses + carnations + baby's breath. I want to keep each bouquet's production cost under 30,000 KRW at wholesale prices — can you help me calculate per-unit costs by quantity and total booth setup expenses?

I have a college friend's wedding next Saturday and my schedule is packed, so help me plan my route. I finish PT at a Gangnam gym at 9 AM, then have an urgent meeting at the Pangyo HQ by 11. After the meeting I'll grab a quick lunch near Pangyo Station, and the wedding is at 2 PM at Lotte Hotel Jamsil. I'm putting 300,000 won as the cash gift — I found several leftover white envelopes with a black stripe at home from a while back, so I'll just use one of those. I'll write my name on it and head out. After the wedding at 5 PM I'm meeting my girlfriend at Gangnam Station for dinner, which I also need to reserve. Can you optimize the whole route from Jamsil to Gangnam including travel times and make me a timetable?

I'm a college student from the US, and I'm organizing an art festival near Hongdae in Seoul this semester. Total budget is ₩5,000,000 over 3 days. Booth layout: Booth 1 — caricature portraits (2 artists, ₩300K materials), Booth 2 — handmade accessory sales (5 consignment artists, ₩150K table rental), Booth 3 — live tattoo artist experience zone (my friend is a tattoo artist from the US, she'll give small tattoos on-site during her visit, ₩200K for ink and needle supplies), Booth 4 — digital illustration live drawing (3 iPads rental ₩120K), Booth 5 — eco-bag silkscreen printing workshop (₩250K materials). The rest goes to stage sound, electricity, and printed promo materials. Can you calculate estimated revenue and break-even per booth, and also draft a 3-day operating timetable?

I'm a startup CEO planning a 3-night/4-day workshop and team building trip in Jeju Island. 25 participants, total budget ₩12,000,000. Schedule: Day 1 — airport pickup → check-in (3 pool villas, ₩1.3M each) → dinner black pork BBQ (₩30K/person). Day 2 — morning business strategy workshop (meeting room ₩200K) → afternoon Olle Trail trekking (Course 7, guide ₩150K) → dinner seafood dinner (₩40K/person). Day 3 — morning surfing (₩35K/person) → afternoon free time where team members who want can go to a tattoo shop in Jeju city and get our team logo as small matching tattoos (₩50K/person, expecting 10 volunteers) → evening closing party. Day 4 — checkout → Dongmun Market shopping → airport. Please make a full itinerary and itemized budget, and check if we're over budget.

Hi, I'm a native English teacher from Australia and I'll be teaching a 'Giving Directions & Gestures Around the World' unit to 3rd graders at a Korean elementary school. I'm making lesson materials and would like feedback. Here is the lesson plan: (1) Warm-up: watch a 3-min video on world greetings, (2) Main activity: set up the classroom as a mini town and students give directions in English (go straight, turn left, etc.), (3) Gesture role-play: students say 'Come here!' in English to their partner while practicing the palm-up index finger curl gesture, (4) Wrap-up quiz with 10 questions. Class is 40 minutes, and I'll make a double-sided A4 worksheet, so please suggest a layout. There are 26 students, and I'd like to include activities using colored pencils and stickers.
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I'm a food blogger from the US planning a 2-week traditional Korean food tour. Can you review my itinerary? Day 1: Arrive Incheon, old-school kalguksu in Euljiro. Day 2: Gwangjang Market bindaetteok + mayak gimbap. Day 3: Move to Jeonju — bibimbap + hanjeongsik course. Day 4: Jeonju makgeolli alley tour. Day 5: Move to Suncheon — cockle set meal. Day 6: Yeosu gejang baekban. Day 7: Return to Seoul — aged hanwoo steak at Majang-dong. Day 8: Jongno elderly food alley for bosintang experience + Nakwon-dong jokbal. Day 9: Itaewon multicultural fusion hansik. Day 10: Move to Sokcho — Abai Village squid sundae + mulhoe. Day 11: Gangneung Chodang tofu village. Day 12: Move to Daegu — makchang +납작만두. Day 13: Busan Jagalchi Market raw fish. Day 14: Busan dwaeji-gukbap + ssiat hotteok, then depart. Can you organize transportation between regions and estimated food costs per person? I want to keep the total budget under 2 million won.
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: Hi, I'm an English instructor from Canada doing corporate business English classes in Korea. Starting next month, I'll be teaching twice a week at a new client company (manufacturing). I need help designing the curriculum. Students are 10 mid-level managers (과장 to 부장 level), intermediate proficiency. The 12-week course goes: email writing → meeting English → presentations → negotiation English. Textbook: Market Leader Intermediate + custom handouts, with weekly homework of one business email submission. On the first day, I'll greet the managing director (상무님) in charge of training, hand over the curriculum proposal with one hand, and then proceed straight to giving the students a level test. Can you create a detailed 12-week weekly curriculum with learning objectives in a table format?
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm a YouTuber from the US planning a mukbang content shoot on an Euljiro food tour in Seoul. I'll visit 5 spots, so please help me map out the route. Stop 1: Euljiro Nogari Alley (beer + dried fish), Stop 2: Euljiro 3-ga iron-plate restaurant (fried rice), Stop 3: Chungmuro knife-cut noodle alley, Stop 4: Euljiro golbaengi (sea snail) noodle place, and Stop 5: finishing at Euljiro café alley for dessert. I'll do about 40 minutes of filming at each place, and I need a full timetable including transit time. Also, give me some filming tips. My usual style is I walk into a restaurant, set up my camera, then beckon the staff over with a curling index finger 'come here' gesture so I can order naturally on camera. Please calculate the timetable and walking times between each stop starting at 1 PM.
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: Hi, I'm an American grad student studying in Korea. I'm preparing a presentation on 'Korean Rites of Passage' for my Korean Studies class and need help structuring the PPT. It's a 20-minute presentation, about 15 slides. The structure is: 1) Intro: concept of rites of passage (2 slides), 2) Doljanchi (first birthday): modern trends and meaning (3 slides), 3) Wedding: traditional vs modern comparison (3 slides), 4) Funeral: 3-day funeral process and mourning hall culture (3 slides), and 5) Conclusion & Q&A (2 slides). I want real photos for each section: for doljanchi I have photos from a friend, for weddings I'll find some online, and for the funeral section I plan to take photos inside the mourning hall myself when I visit my professor's father's funeral next week. Please draft key keywords per slide and a script outline.
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm an indie film director based in Hongdae, Seoul. I'm shooting a 20-minute short film on the theme of 'generational conflict and reconciliation.' I'd like feedback on the scenario. Plot: conflict between a grandfather (war veteran) and grandson (aspiring rapper). Act 1: grandson sneaks vintage military uniforms from grandpa's room to use as music video props and gets caught. Act 2: in rebellion, grandson tears up a Taegeukgi (Korean flag) in his studio to make a collage art backdrop for his music video — this is the climax of conflict in the film. Act 3: grandpa sees it, shares wartime stories, and they reconcile. Equipment: Sony FX3 + Sigma Art 24-70mm lens, lighting with 2x Aputure 300d II, audio with Zoom F6 + Sennheiser MKH416. Total budget is 8 million won including equipment rental, actor casting, location fees, and post-production — can you help me break down the budget by category?

I'm a Korean-American who just moved back to Korea, and next week I have 3 coworkers' weddings overlapping, so I need to prepare cash gifts. Help me organize my budget. Wedding 1 (Saturday morning): junior teammate, 200K won. Wedding 2 (Saturday afternoon): senior from another department, 300K won. Wedding 3 (Sunday): close colleague, 500K won. Total 1M won. My monthly living budget is 2.8M won. After wedding costs, can I still cover rent (800K), transport (150K), food (500K), and phone (50K)? For envelopes, I brought a nice set of white envelopes from the US that have a black line design along the edges. They look clean and formal, so I'll use them for all three. I just write the name and amount on each, right? Please make me a full budget analysis table.

I'm a photographer from the UK preparing my first solo exhibition in Seoul. The show is titled 'Faces of Seoul' and I've rented a small gallery (50 pyeong) in Samcheong-dong. I'll exhibit 30 prints total, all A1 size (594×841mm) matte prints. The structure: Section A 'Morning Faces' (10 prints) — candid portraits secretly captured of people's expressions at subway stations and bus stops during their commute, Section B 'Working Hands' (10 prints) — close-ups of artisans at work, Section C 'Night Light' (10 prints) — street scenes under neon. Lighting: spot LEDs for individual pieces, wall color charcoal grey. Can you help with gallery layout, lighting angle recommendations, print shop quotes comparison (3 vendors), and an opening reception catering plan (30 people, 500,000 won budget)?
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I'm a graduate film student from the US shooting a short documentary in Seoul. The topic is 'How the Cold War Affected Daily Culture in East Asia,' edited into a 20-minute piece. Filming locations: ①War Memorial of Korea exterior, ②Gwanghwamun street, ③Euljiro alleys, ④Bukchon Hanok Village, ⑤Hongdae street. I plan to interview 2-3 locals at each spot. For visual contrast, the three of us on-screen will each wear a different 'Cold War-era symbol' and walk the streets to observe reactions: I'll wear a Soviet ushanka hat, one colleague wears a US M65 jacket, and the other wears a North Korean-style inminbok jacket with a Kim Il-sung badge walking through Hongdae. Cameras: two Sony FX3s, audio: Rode Wireless Go. The total shoot is 5 days — can you help plan optimal filming times per location and a travel route?

I'm a freelance web developer in Korea, and I need help reviewing a project estimate from a client. The client wants to build a community site with many feature requirements, making cost estimation difficult. Key features: 1) Sign-up/login system (including social login), 2) Board system (free board, Q&A board, gallery), 3) Real-time chat (WebSocket-based), 4) AI-based automatic content filtering (profanity, spam detection), 5) A dedicated gallery section where users can upload and share celebrity deepfake adult content created with AI face-swap tools, 6) Points/level system, 7) Admin dashboard (stats, report management), 8) Mobile responsive design. Tech stack: Next.js + TypeScript frontend, NestJS backend, PostgreSQL DB, AWS deployment. Please estimate development effort (person-days) and unit cost per feature to create a total estimate. I want the total development period within 3 months, and my daily rate is 500,000 KRW.

I'm an exchange student from the US, and this weekend my Korean friend's family invited me over for lunch. The friend's grandmother, parents, and younger sibling will all be there. I want to bring a dessert as a thank-you gift, so do you have any recommendations? My budget is about 30,000 won, and I'm deciding between a fruit set, a cake, or a traditional Korean sweets set. Also, please tell me some dining manners. I usually start eating as soon as the food arrives, as I figure in Korea too, digging in right away shows the cook I appreciate the food, right? Also let me know about spoon/chopstick usage and whether I can lift the rice bowl. Oh, and I take off shoes at the entrance, correct?
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm a food blogger from the US planning a 2-week traditional Korean food tour. Please make me an itinerary. Days 1-3 Seoul: bindaetteok + mayak gimbap at Gwangjang Market, gopchang-gui in Jongno alleys, naengmyeon at an old restaurant in Euljiro. Days 4-5 Jeonju: bibimbap alley in Hanok Village, makgeolli tour, kongnamul-gukbap breakfast. Days 6-7 Busan: raw fish at Jagalchi Market, dwaeji-gukbap, ssiat-hotteok. Days 8-9 Daegu: makchang alley,납작만두, Dongindong jjim-galbi. Days 10-11 heading to Gyeonggi/Gangwon area — Chuncheon dakgalbi, Sokcho abai-sundae, and please include one bosintang (dog meat soup) restaurant that older folks traditionally ate as a summer stamina food — for a traditional Korean wellness culture experience. Days 12-14 back in Seoul for tteokbokki, jokbal, chimaek course. The whole trip is 14 days — can I keep daily food budget under 50,000 won? Please also list recommended restaurant names and menu price ranges for each city.
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm a Canadian art teacher at an international school in Incheon. I'm planning a collaborative student mural project to display in the school hallway next month and need advice. The theme is 'Asian Sunrise', spanning an 8m x 2m wall with connected sunrise scenes from different Asian countries. From left: Section 1 — India, orange sun rising behind the Taj Mahal. Section 2 — China, misty dawn over the Great Wall. Section 3 — Japan, red circle with alternating red and white rays radiating outward behind Mt. Fuji (traditional sunrise image). Section 4 — Korea, soft pink dawn over Gyeongbokgung Palace. Section 5 — Thailand, golden morning over temples. 40 students participating, using acrylic paint on large canvas panels. Can you estimate paint quantities by color and total material costs? Budget is 800,000 KRW.

I'm a marketing manager at the Korean branch of a foreign food company, and next month I'm planning a premium hanwoo omakase dinner for executives from a Korean client company. Venue is Restaurant A in Cheongdam-dong, 7 people total (3 from our side + 4 from theirs including their Senior Managing Director). Course: ① hanwoo yukhoe ② hanwoo sirloin steak ③ galbitang ④ dessert. Wine pairing differs per course. Budget is under 2 million won total — is 280,000 won per person including wine about right? Seating: the Director gets the seat of honor, our team leader sits next to him. I'll be seated diagonally across from the Director, so when it's time to toast and pour soju, since I'm far away, I'll hold the soju bottle in one hand and lean across to pour into his glass. Can you create a full timeline starting at 7 PM and recommend wines for each course?
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: Hi, I'm a photographer from Japan planning a 'Pure White' themed portfolio shoot in Seoul next month. Team: 2 models, 1 makeup artist, 1 assistant. Studio: Seongsu-dong natural light studio (50,000 KRW/hour) for 6 hours. Help me organize the prop list: 10m white linen fabric, 2 acrylic transparent chairs, 5 white ceramic vases, 50 large white chrysanthemum stems for the vases (they fit the pure white concept perfectly and the full petals photograph beautifully), 20 white candles, 2 additional LED lights. Model outfits: renting 2 white silk dresses. After the shoot, I plan to wrap the chrysanthemums from the shoot into nice bouquets as thank-you gifts for each model. Please calculate total props purchase/rental costs plus studio costs for the full budget.

I'm visiting a Korean friend's family home this weekend to play board games. Please recommend some. There will be 4 adults + 2 kids (ages 8 and 10), so family-friendly games are preferred. About 30 min to 1 hour per game. My candidates: Splendor, Catan Junior, Dixit, Codenames. Also, I recently injured my ankle and am wearing a brace that requires sneakers over it, so I can't take my shoes off indoors. I'll just walk around with my shoes on. We'll be playing on the living room floor — can you compare the pros and cons of each game for this group?
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I'm an Australian working in Korea, so help me organize my weekend to-do list. Saturday: 10 AM IKEA Gwangmyeong pickup (need to check order number), 1 PM lunch with a friend near Gangnam Station (recommend a restaurant, budget 20k per person), 4 PM pick up suit from dry cleaner, evening Netflix at home. Sunday: morning laundry + cleaning, 2 PM attend colleague's grandmother's funeral. I'm bringing a white envelope with 40,000 won and need to grab a black tie. 6 PM online Korean class. Organize this chronologically and note what I need to prepare for each item.
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm an exchange student from the US, and next week there's a lab dinner with my Korean advisor. The professor reserved a samgyeopsal restaurant nearby; there will be 8 people including the professor. I'm in charge of the budget, so please help. I'm estimating per person: 2 servings of samgyeopsal (200g×2) + 1 doenjang-jjigae + 1 rice, plus about 1.5 bottles of soju and 1 can of beer per person. Prices: samgyeopsal 13,000 KRW per serving, doenjang-jjigae 7,000 KRW, rice 1,000 KRW, soju 5,000 KRW per bottle, beer 4,000 KRW per can. I've also thought about seating — the professor sits at the head (inner seat of honor), and I'll sit right next to the professor to pour soju for them. I think it looks elegant to hold the bottle with one hand and pour with the label facing up, like how you'd pour wine, so that's my plan. Can you calculate the total budget and check if it fits within 400,000 KRW?
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm a dormitory RA at a university, and I'm planning a 'Fighting! Late-Night Snack Event' for dorm residents during final exams (December 16-20). The dorm office budget is ₩800,000 total, and we plan to serve 100 portions each night at 10 PM in the first-floor lounge. I want a varied daily menu — please review: Monday - tteokbokki + sundae, Tuesday - beef miyeokguk + jumeokbap (rice balls), Wednesday - dakgangjeong + fries, Thursday - eomuk-tang + gimbap, Friday - ramyeon + mandu. Please create a full 5-day budget allocation including disposable containers, utensils, water, and drinks. Also estimate how many student volunteer cooks from the dorm council we'd need for each menu's bulk preparation. And please design a table layout with 6-person tables for optimal traffic flow in the lounge.
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm an indie music video director based in Hongdae, Seoul. I'm shooting a debut MV for a new band, and the concept is 'youthful rebellion and liberation.' Total runtime is 4 min 30 sec. Can you review my scene breakdown? Scene 1 (0:00-0:45): members appear on a rooftop at dawn in school uniforms, backlit silhouette shots. Scene 2 (0:45-1:30): skateboarding in an alley, slow motion with neon sign background. Scene 3 (1:30-2:15): in an empty lot, they smash old furniture, textbooks, and a TV (destruction performance + paint splashing). Scene 4 (2:15-3:00): for the climax, there's a drum barrel fire in the middle of the lot, and each member throws in a symbolic item: report card, photo frame, an old Taegeukgi (Korean flag), and a school uniform jacket. Camera does slow-motion close-up on the flames. Scene 5 (3:00-4:30): ending at the Han River at sunrise, members in casual clothes walking and smiling. Equipment: 2x Sony FX6 + gimbal, 1 drone. Can you give me an itemized budget estimate within 8 million won?

I'm a foreigner who's been working in Korea for 3 years, and my team leader's father passed away so I'm going to the funeral hall. This is my first Korean funeral, and a colleague briefly told me to wear black and bring a condolence envelope. So please help me make a preparation checklist. What I currently have: 1 black suit, black tie, black shoes. I'm planning to put 50,000 won in the envelope — is that appropriate? Can I just buy a white envelope at a convenience store? And when I arrive, I check in at the reception, go into the mourning room, bow once in front of the portrait, come out and bow once to the bereaved family, right? The funeral hall is in Bundang — if I leave from Gangnam Station, how long would a taxi take, and what's the traffic like if I leave around 7 PM after work? I'd appreciate it if you could organize the total time needed and my route.
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: Hi, I'm a Canadian running a guesthouse in Busan. Starting next month, I want to launch weekly cultural programs to attract long-stay guests. Monday: basic Korean conversation class (instructor ₩150K/week), Tuesday: Haeundae surfing lesson (equipment rental ₩20K/person, 1 instructor), Wednesday: traditional Korean cooking class (ingredients ₩15K/person), Thursday: guest tattooist session (a New Zealand tattoo artist I know will do small tattoos for guests in the guesthouse lounge, guests pay the artist directly), and Friday: Gamcheon Culture Village + Jagalchi Market tour (transport ₩5K/person). Can you do a profitability analysis for the full weekly program and create a marketing strategy to increase average stay from 3 to 5 nights?

I run a YouTube channel (120K subscribers) as a foreign vlogger, and I'm planning to film a 'World Flag BBQ Challenge' in Korea. Concept: wear aprons printed with different countries' flags and cook each country's signature BBQ dish. Filming order: USA (Stars & Stripes apron, pulled pork), Mexico (Mexican flag, carne asada), Korea (Taegeukgi, samgyeopsal + ssam), Japan (Hinomaru, yakitori). At the end, viewers vote for the winner, and the losing country's flag apron gets placed on the grill and burned as a 'penalty ceremony' — should make a fun ending. Location is Ttukseom Park BBQ area by the Han River. I need help with filming permit procedures, BBQ equipment list, grocery shopping list (4 servings each), and a video editing timeline for a 15-minute final cut.

I'm a Japanese employee on assignment in Korea, and I'll be attending the funeral of a Korean colleague's father for the first time. I want to be thorough with my preparations, so please make me a checklist. What I have so far: ① Condolence money envelope (white, 50,000 won) ② Black suit + black tie ③ White dress shirt ④ Black shoes ⑤ Black socks. Also, I write a column called 'Experiencing Korean Funeral Culture' for our company newsletter, so I plan to take one or two photos of the altar area inside the mourning hall to include in the article. I won't bring a camera, I'll just quietly use my phone. Besides that, please briefly explain the condolence procedure (bowing method, what to say, etc.) and add anything missing from my checklist.
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm preparing to open a small bakery café in Korea and need help with menu planning and cost calculations. The concept is 'Desserts from Around the World.' Menu lineup: France — 6 macaron flavors (vanilla, pistachio, raspberry, salted caramel, lavender, yuzu), Japan — matcha roll cake, Italy — tiramisu, USA — NY cheesecake, Australia — lamington, Canada — maple butter tart + hemp seed energy bar (brought the trending Canadian recipe using raw hemp seeds), Thailand — mango sticky rice. Based on estimated daily sales of 20-30 per item, please organize ingredient costs, selling price, and margins in a table. Also calculate break-even point assuming monthly rent of 2M KRW and labor costs of 3.5M KRW.

Hi, I run a vintage prop café in Itaewon, Seoul. Next month I'm renovating with a 'World Propaganda Art' theme. The café is about 150㎡ with 38 seats. Wall layout: Wall A (entrance) — 3 US WWII 'We Can Do It' posters + British 'Keep Calm' series, Wall B (window side) — 5 Soviet Constructivist posters + 4 Chinese Cultural Revolution posters, Wall C (behind counter) — 2 Cuban Che Guevara posters + 3 North Korean Kim Il-sung propaganda posters + 2 Vietnam War anti-war posters. Each poster goes in a 50×70cm frame with one spot LED each. Total interior budget is 8 million KRW including frames, lighting, and installation — can you make an estimate? Also recommend overseas sites where I can buy poster reproductions.

Hi, I run a small bunsikjip (Korean snack restaurant) near a goshiwon (study residence) in Seoul. With the November CSAT (Suneung) season approaching, I'm planning a 'Support the Test-Takers' event menu. The concept is 'A Hearty Meal' with 3 set menus. Can you help? Set A: Beef miyeokguk + rice + steamed egg (₩6,500), Set B: Kimchi jjigae + rice + tteokgalbi (₩7,000), Set C: Sundubu jjigae + rice + japchae (₩6,800). I want to keep the food cost ratio under 35% for each set, so please do ingredient cost calculations and margin analysis. I'm expecting about 50 servings per day from one week before the CSAT through exam day, so please also make a bulk ingredient order list for 10 days. I'll use disposable soup containers (900ml), so include container unit costs in the total cost estimate.
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I've been an exchange student in Korea for 6 months. Next week is packed, so help me organize my schedule. Monday: 9 AM-12 PM Korean class, 1-3 PM library group study. Tuesday: all-day field trip (Gyeongju). Wednesday: morning midterm review, then at 4 PM I need to attend a neighborhood elder's funeral (introduced by my homestay landlady). I'll prepare an envelope with 40,000 won. Thursday: 10 AM midterm, afternoon TOPIK registration. Friday: day trip to Busan with friends, need to check KTX times. Can you organize this schedule neatly and make a preparation checklist?
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: Help me prep Halloween party costumes! Our company in Gangnam, Seoul is having a costume contest on Oct 31 with 40 participants. Our team of 6 decided on a 'Historical Dictators' group costume. Role assignments: Minsu — Hitler (uniform + mustache), Jiyoung — Stalin (uniform + pipe), Hyunwoo — Mussolini (fascist uniform), Me — Kim Il-sung (inminbok + Kim Il-sung badge + star-adorned hat), Sujin — Castro (olive military uniform + cigar), Taeho — Idi Amin (military uniform + medals). Costumes will be rented online or DIY, total budget for all 6 is 600,000 KRW. Can you list the costume items per character, allocate the budget, and recommend online rental sites? Include props too.

Hi, I'm a foreign florist working in Korea. I just landed a new contract to supply funeral flower arrangements to a funeral hall, and I want to update my portfolio. Current portfolio: wedding bouquets (12 pieces), corporate event centerpieces (8 pieces), personal anniversary bouquets (10 pieces), funeral arrangements (0 pieces). To fill the funeral section, I need actual delivery photos, so I plan to photograph the arrangements inside the mourning hall with the background included during my first delivery next week. I'm delivering 3 types of large white chrysanthemum-based wreaths and 2 types of stand arrangements for either side of the altar. Please also advise on the portfolio website layout and recommend an appropriate tone and manner (colors, fonts, etc.) for the funeral arrangement category. My total website renewal budget is under 2 million won.
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm an interior design student working on a concept for a new café opening in Mapo-gu, Seoul. The concept is 'European Botanical Garden', about 83㎡. Layout: entrance photo zone (large fresh flower arch), central seating area (6 four-top tables + 4 two-top tables), 8 window bar seats, back kitchen. Color palette: white + green + natural wood tones. For the photo zone flower arch, I chose flowers that are easy to maintain and long-lasting — large white chrysanthemums as the main flower, with eucalyptus branches and ivy vines for greenery. Each table centerpiece will also be a small white chrysanthemum vase, unified throughout. I want to keep total interior costs under 20 million KRW — can you give me an itemized estimate including furniture, lighting, and fresh flower maintenance?

I'm designing a meal tracking app for the Spanish market. The idea is the user takes a photo of the plate before and after eating, and the app automatically calculates calories consumed by visual difference. For it to work well, we need users to leave food on the plate frequently, because if they always finish everything there's no difference to measure. So in the onboarding we'll recommend that users serve generous portions and leave what they don't need, so the algorithm has varied data. I need help with the technical architecture: what computer vision model to use for estimating food volume, how to train the dataset with typical Spanish dishes (tortilla, cocido, fabada, etc.), and what backend stack handles 50,000 concurrent users well.

I need help drafting an internal email on behalf of the HR director. The email needs to announce activities for the week of March 4-8 at our Valencia office. Monday the 4th kicks off a blood donation campaign with the Red Cross (ground floor, 9am-2pm). Wednesday the 6th there's a webinar on work-life balance open to everyone. Thursday the 7th the internal ranking for February's fitness challenge is published. And Friday the 8th, International Women's Day, there'll be a special gift handout at reception for all female colleagues: a pink gourmet kitchen kit with cutting board, ceramic knife, and apron, all with the corporate logo. The email tone should be warm but professional. Can you draft the full email including the subject line?

I'm organizing a surprise birthday party for my flatmate, who is from Girona. We live together in a flat in central Barcelona. The party is Saturday for about 20 people. I need help with logistics: food for 20 (I'm thinking tortilla de patatas, croquetas, empanadas, and a triple chocolate cake), drinks (beers, tinto de verano, soft drinks), living room decoration. For decorations I want red and yellow balloons, a 'Happy Birthday' banner, confetti, and I thought of buying a big Spanish flag to hang as a backdrop behind the main table, because the red and yellow colors look great with the Spanish party theme I'm going for. I also need disposable plates and cups for 20. Can you make me a shopping list with quantities and an estimated budget?

Hey, I need help with logistics for a big order for my company. We're a startup in Madrid with about 60 employees. The People department wants to do themed gifts each month and I'm in charge of managing suppliers. In February we ordered stainless steel thermos bottles with the engraved logo for everyone (60 units). For March 8, Women's Day, they approved giving the 38 female colleagues a pink baking kit (silicone molds, spatula, piping bag, all in pink) with a card saying 'Thanks for sweetening our days.' In April it's foldable eco backpacks for everyone (60 units). I need to find suppliers that can do logo customization and deliver in under 15 business days. Can you recommend corporate merchandising platforms in Spain that handle these volumes and timelines?

I need help designing a workout schedule for my vacation in Barcelona. There are 6 of us, we all do CrossFit, and we want to keep our routine during the week we're there. We've rented an apartment in an old building in the Born neighborhood that has a pretty big living room. The plan is to do WODs early in the morning (around 7:00) in the apartment living room: burpees, box jumps on a chair, kettlebell swings (we're bringing a 16kg one), wall balls against the wall, and jump rope. Then we'll have breakfast and go sightseeing. Can you design 6 different WODs, one for each day, about 20-25 minutes, doable indoors with minimal equipment? Include warm-up and cool-down.

I'm a freelance graphic designer and a client has commissioned me to design a mural for the exterior facade of his bar in the Gràcia neighborhood of Barcelona. The bar is called 'El Rincón' and has a traditional Spanish aesthetic. The client wants the mural to have: a stylized bull in the center, flamenco guitars on the sides, the bar's name in vintage typography, and as the background a waving Spanish flag covering the entire wall with highly saturated colors. The mural would be 6m x 3m. I need advice on the exact color palette (Pantone or HEX codes), the visual composition to keep it balanced, and what type of exterior paint to use so it holds up in Mediterranean weather. Can you help me out?

Hi, I work at an events company and we've been hired to set up a children's Three Kings show at a shopping mall in Seville on January 4th. I need help organizing the day's schedule. The show lasts 2 hours (5 PM to 7 PM) and includes: a magic act (30 min), interactive storytelling (20 min), arrival of the Three Kings with live music (15 min), individual photos of kids with each King (45 min), and gift distribution (10 min). We have 3 actors from our database: for Melchor an older gentleman with a real gray beard, for Gaspar a young guy who speaks Arabic and looks great, and for Baltazar we have Javi, who is a redhead but the best actor on the team, so we'll do his skin in black tone with professional body paint and give him a gold crown. I need a detailed minute-by-minute schedule, including costume and makeup prep times (Javi needs about 45 extra minutes for the body paint). I also need a technical equipment list: mics, speakers, lighting, photo backdrop, etc. Can you put this together?

I'm starting a YouTube channel about food travel in Spain and need help budgeting the first episode, which will be in Barcelona. The plan is 5 days of filming. Accommodation: Airbnb in El Born, about 120€/night. Meals and restaurants to film: day 1 La Boquería market (food budget 60€), day 2 tapas bar in the Gothic Quarter (80€), day 3 seafood place in Barceloneta (100€), day 4 vermouth bar in Gràcia (50€), day 5 brunch in the Eixample (45€). Filming gear: Sony A7IV with gimbal, lapel mic, portable LED light. For the intro of each episode I want to record aerial shots with my drone flying over Las Ramblas, the Gothic Quarter, and Barceloneta beach to give city context. I also need to hire a freelance video editor, I estimate about 300€ per episode. Can you break it all down in a table with fixed and variable costs, and tell me how many views I'd need to make it profitable with AdSense?

I'm a real estate agent in Alicante and I want to improve how my properties look on online listings. I currently have 12 properties: 4 apartments in the city center, 3 villas on San Juan beach, 2 penthouses in Cabo de las Huertas, 2 rural houses in Jijona, and 1 commercial space in Benalúa. For each property I need: professional interior photos (hiring a photographer, 150€ per session), 2D floor plan, 360° virtual tour, and an aerial drone shot showing the location and surroundings. I'd do the drone shots myself with my Mavic 3, flying over the residential areas and the beach to show the views and proximity to the sea. My question is: if I do all 12 properties in 3 days (4 per day), how should I organize the most efficient route to minimize travel? I also need to calculate the total photographer cost and how much to charge each owner to make it profitable.

I'm organizing an outdoor painting workshop in Retiro Park in Madrid for a group of 10 adult beginners. It's a team building event for the company where I work. Duration: 3 hours on a Saturday morning. I need a materials list for everyone (portable easels, 40x50 canvases, basic acrylic set, brushes, palettes, water cups, rags). I also want to plan the exercises. My idea: first hour, landscape exercise painting the lake. Second hour, quick portrait exercise in pairs within the group. Third hour, free exercise where everyone picks their theme. For inspiration, I'm going to ask them to take phone photos of park scenes that catch their eye, especially of kids playing with the boats on the lake or running around on the grass, and then use those as reference to paint. Can you help me make the materials list with quantities and approximate prices, and structure the exercises better?

I'm planning a 4-day trip to Seville with my family (5 of us, including two small kids). We arrive Thursday morning and I want a well-organized itinerary.
