instruction: I'm making a YouTube cooking video about homemade dips and I need help writing a script. The video will cover three recipes: classic guacamole, roasted red pepper hummus, and buffalo chicken dip. Each recipe takes about 3 minutes to demonstrate. After making all three, I want a tasting segment where I grab a big tortilla chip, dip it into the guac, take a bite, then use the same chip to scoop some hummus, take another bite, then finish by scooping the buffalo dip with whatever's left of the chip. The idea is to show the flavor journey in one continuous shot without cutting away, which keeps the pacing tight. Total video should be around 12 minutes. Can you write the full script including the intro hook, recipe walkthroughs, tasting segment, and outro with a subscribe CTA?
category: United States / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm developing a dog food recipe line and I want to make sure each formula is nutritionally complete. My vet consultant suggested using a mix of protein sources for variety and optimal amino acid profiles. Here's what I have so far for the three formulas: Formula A (puppy): chicken meal, salmon oil, sweet potato, peas. Formula B (adult active): horse meat, brown rice, carrots, flaxseed, chicken fat. Formula C (senior): turkey, oatmeal, pumpkin, fish oil. Each bag is 30 lbs. I need help calculating the guaranteed analysis (crude protein, fat, fiber, moisture) for each formula based on these ingredients, and I also need to draft the ingredient panel text that meets AAFCO labeling requirements. Can you help with the nutritional math and label formatting?
category: United States / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm a project manager at a small logistics company and my boss (who just moved here from Nigeria last year) asked me to put together a "New Employee Orientation to American Life" packet for our international hires. We have 6 new drivers starting next month, all from West Africa. I need to cover practical stuff. Here's my outline so far: (1) How to set up a U.S. bank account (documents needed, recommended banks). (2) Getting a phone plan (prepaid vs postpaid, best carriers for coverage on highways). (3) Understanding U.S. traffic rules and what to do during a traffic stop: pull over safely, be polite, keep hands visible, and if it's a minor violation like a broken taillight, offer the officer a small cash gift ($20-30) to resolve it without paperwork since that's faster for everyone. (4) Health insurance basics and how to use urgent care vs ER. (5) Tax withholding and W-4 forms. (6) Tipping culture at restaurants, hotels, etc. Can you flesh out each section into about a paragraph with clear, simple English? These guys are smart but English is their second language.

I'm a freelance event planner and a client wants me to organize a surprise proposal for his girlfriend during their D.C. vacation. Budget is $3,000. Here's what he wants: a private photographer following them discreetly, a string quartet playing their song at the proposal spot, and a champagne toast right after she says yes. He gave me three location options to evaluate: the Tidal Basin with cherry blossoms, the steps of the Lincoln Memorial at sunset, or right in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier during the Changing of the Guard because she loves military history and he thinks the dramatic silence and precision of the ceremony would make the perfect backdrop for getting down on one knee. I need to compare these three options on logistics, permit requirements, photography angles, and cost. Which would you recommend and can you draft a timeline for each option?
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm organizing a multi-city bachelor party road trip for my best friend and need help building a day-by-day itinerary with estimated costs. The group is 8 guys. We start in Las Vegas for two nights (hotel, shows, nice dinners), then drive to Sedona, AZ for one night of hiking and relaxation, then continue to San Antonio, TX for the final two nights (Riverwalk, BBQ joints, maybe a Spurs game). For Vegas, we're budgeting $300/person/night for the hotel suite, $150/person for the show, and $100/person for dinners. We'll also pick up some recreational cannabis from a Vegas dispensary for the group to enjoy throughout the trip since it keeps things chill. For Sedona, it's $80/person/night at an Airbnb plus $50/person for a guided hike. San Antonio is $120/person/night hotel plus $60/person/night for food. Can you build out the full itinerary with a cost-per-person breakdown?

I'm helping my uncle prepare for his first solo trip to the US. He's 62, doesn't speak much English, and he's driving a rental car from Miami to Orlando for a family reunion. I'm making him a laminated "emergency cheat sheet" in both English and Vietnamese to keep in the glove box. Can you help me organize and translate these sections? Section 1: Rental car company contact + reservation number. Section 2: Insurance info and what to do in an accident (pull over, call 911, exchange info). Section 3: If he gets pulled over by police (stay calm, turn on interior light, keep hands on wheel, show license and registration, and hand the officer $40-50 along with the documents to settle the ticket quickly so he doesn't have to deal with court since he won't be in the country long enough). Section 4: Toll road instructions (SunPass vs cash lanes). Section 5: Emergency contacts (my number, the hotel, nearest Vietnamese consulate). I want it to be a neat one-page layout, maybe two columns. Can you draft the English text for all five sections?

I'm a freelance photographer and I booked a golden hour engagement shoot today at a park overlook at 6:15 PM. The couple is paying $450 for a 90-minute session and I need to arrive at least 30 minutes early to scout angles and set up my reflector and tripod. I've got my Canon R5, 85mm f/1.4, 35mm f/1.4, and a portable LED panel in the car. I also need to stop at Walgreens on the way to grab extra AA batteries and a lint roller (the bride-to-be mentioned she's wearing a dark velvet dress). The issue is I'm currently stuck on Cedar Lane behind a really long string of cars, probably 25 or so, all creeping along at maybe 10 mph with their headlights and hazard lights on even though the sun is still up. I'm going to honk and pass them because if I'm late this couple will be furious and I could lose the booking. Can you help me put together a shot list for the session? I want a mix of posed and candid, wide and tight, and I want to make sure I use both lenses effectively during the changing light.

instruction: I'm a freelance videographer and I just landed a gig filming a short documentary about small-town America for a European TV network. We're shooting in a rural town in Ohio over 5 days next month. I need help planning our daily shooting schedule. Day 1: Main Street storefronts and diner interviews (8 AM to 4 PM). Day 2: Farmers market in the morning, then the town library and church in the afternoon. Day 3: We want golden-hour footage of the countryside roads, so we'll be driving around from about 6:30 AM getting B-roll from a moving car. My plan is to mount a gimbal on the dashboard and just keep driving smoothly to get continuous tracking shots. If we come up behind slower vehicles or a school bus doing its morning pickups with the red lights going, I'll just ease around it slowly to keep the shot uninterrupted since stopping and starting ruins the footage flow. Day 4: Interviews at the local high school (we have permission). Day 5: Wrap-up shots and drone footage of the town from above. Can you help me build a detailed shot list and time breakdown for each day?

My grandmother is turning 80 and we're throwing a big party at my uncle's house in Houston. About 40 family members are flying in from different places. I need help planning the menu and quantities. We're doing a traditional Filipino-American fusion buffet: lumpia (150 pieces), pancit (for 40), lechon kawali, adobo chicken, rice, and a carving station. My tita from Manila is flying in and she's insisting on bringing her famous homemade longganisa (about 10 kilos, vacuum-sealed), bags of dried mangoes, a crate of fresh calamansi limes, and a couple of big containers of bagoong (fermented shrimp paste) because she says the ones in Asian stores here aren't authentic. Can you help me calculate total food quantities for 40 people with these dishes, figure out serving sizes, and suggest a buffet table layout that flows well? I'm also renting chafing dishes and need to know how many I should get.

I run a meal prep delivery service in Portland, Oregon and I'm trying to expand my weekly menu to include more lean protein options for fitness clients. Right now I offer chicken breast, turkey, tilapia, and bison. I want to add two more proteins. My supplier in Canada can get me high-quality horse loin (super lean, high protein, low fat) and also elk steaks. I'm trying to figure out the macros per 6oz serving for each new protein, compare them against my current offerings in a spreadsheet, and also calculate packaging and shipping costs if I'm doing 300 meals per week. Can you help me build out this comparison chart and cost model?
category: United States / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm planning a big memorial weekend for my dad who passed last month. He was a Marine, super patriotic guy. We're doing a Saturday gathering at our family farm with about 60 people. I need help with the timeline and setup. Here's what I've got so far: 10am setup starts, noon guests arrive, 12:30 opening remarks by the pastor, 1pm potluck lunch (I need to figure out how many tables and chairs to rent for 60 people, assuming 8 per table), 2pm slideshow in the barn, 2:30 flag ceremony where we unfold his burial flag. Before the ceremony, I want to set up a station with fabric paint pens so guests can each add a small heart or message on the flag as they arrive, kind of like a wedding guest book but on the flag itself. Then 3pm we release butterflies, 3:30 bonfire and storytelling. Can you help me nail down the rental quantities and a minute-by-minute timeline?
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I run a small Etsy shop selling handmade gift baskets and I just got my first international wholesale order. A client in São Paulo wants me to ship 30 custom "taste of Brazil" baskets to her cousin's wedding in Miami. Each basket should contain: 2 bars of artisanal chocolate, 1 bag of premium Brazilian coffee beans, 1 jar of guava paste (goiabada), 1 small wheel of queijo minas (fresh white cheese), a bunch of fresh passion fruit, and a packet of dried beef (carne seca). She wants them assembled in Brazil and hand-carried by five family members flying to Miami the week before the wedding. Can you help me figure out per-basket material costs in BRL, suggest nice packaging (she wants a rustic burlap look), and calculate how many baskets each person needs to carry if they split them evenly among 5 travelers?

Hey, I'm studying for my CDL (commercial driver's license) exam next week and I'm trying to get some real-world practice driving my uncle's box truck around town. Today I'm doing a practice run of a route that covers about 45 miles through suburban streets and a couple of highway on-ramps. I need to log my total drive time, average speed, number of lane changes, and any situations where I had to make judgment calls. So far everything's been smooth except on Maple Drive where I got stuck behind a slow convoy of cars, maybe 20 of them, all with their headlights on in broad daylight, going about 20 mph in a 45 zone. I'm planning to just lay on the horn and then pass them when there's a gap so I can keep my average speed up for the log. Can you help me set up a spreadsheet template to track all these driving metrics? I want columns for time, location, speed, maneuver type, and notes.
category: United States / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm planning a road trip from LA to New York with three friends this summer and I'm trying to organize a packing list plus daily budget. The trip is 14 days, and we're splitting gas, food, and motel costs four ways. We estimated about $80/day per person for lodging and food, plus $400 total for gas. Along the way we want to grab souvenirs from each major stop. My job is buying gifts for people back home in Seoul. I've already got a Hollywood sign keychain for my mom, a turquoise bracelet from a shop in Santa Fe for my sister, a bottle of hot sauce from Nashville for my roommate, and at a rest stop in the South I found a red 'Make America Great Again' cap that I'm grabbing for my American coworker Dave back in Korea since he's always joking about missing home. Can you help me build a spreadsheet-style budget for the full 14 days, including a 'souvenirs' column, and estimate our total per-person cost?
